The FoxFibre® Green Weft Selvedge is a 13oz Japanese selvedge denim that pairs indigo rope-dyed warp yarns with a naturally colored FoxFibre® weft. The distinctive green-grey tone comes from natural green FoxFibre® cotton that has been treated with iron, a traditional mineral-based process used to deepen and stabilize naturally occurring color. Rather than adding dye, the iron reacts with the cotton’s inherent pigment, resulting in an earthy green-grey tone that becomes more pronounced with washing and wear.
FoxFibre® was developed by cotton breeder and environmental pioneer Sally Fox, who began her work in the 1980s by selectively breeding naturally pigmented cotton varieties to eliminate the need for conventional dyeing. Because the color is grown into the fiber itself, FoxFibre® significantly reduces the environmental impact associated with chemical dyes and finishing.

Defined by distinctive rectangular pocket stitching, the “Baker” style draws inspiration from the original OG-107 fatigue pants worn by U.S. troops in the 1950s — a wider, more relaxed fit than many of our cuts.
While developing this 13.5oz denim, Shinichi Haraki found inspiration in his favourite pair of Levi’s 646 bell-bottom jeans from the mid-1970s. The warp yarn is rope-dyed indigo in the traditional manner, then sulphur-dyed with a grey dye to impart a darker hue — a technique commonly used by Levi’s at the time. The long slub, neppy warp yarn and natural slub weft create a heavily nepped finish on both the face and reverse of the fabric, resulting in a soft, flexible denim packed with vintage character.
In addition to the unique denim, other key features of these pants include flap-down rear pockets with secure button fastenings, a brass zipper fly, and rear waist cinches—allowing the fit to be adjusted without a belt.
